title: Practise it small, say we, give credit
header_line: My analysis of one book on negotiation. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Where can you try this where nothing is at stake?
I said: always use we, never you or I. We can make this happen. You only use you when you are not even using you; you just say it seems like.
A student asked about it when someone says we and it is really my problem.
I said: authenticity, but be careful, because you want a team situation.
I said to always give other people the credit: every time we do something with you, success is inevitable.
A student said that if you go straight into a business situation using these phrases, it can feel extremely fake, so practise slowly and subtly on friends.
Another said that the first time he tried it at a gym, he saw the look on a man's face at how inauthentic it sounded, and it improved a lot since.
I said: you have to really care, because people pick it up if you do not.
Another suggested picking one person and one statement and saying it genuinely, then layering another once it becomes second nature.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write one person you will practise on.
Write how you will check it sounds true.
Write the next phrase you will layer.

check.q: What did I say to always use?
What did a student say about practising?
What did I say people pick up on?

recap: Say we. Give credit. Practise on low stakes, one phrase at a time.
